deities: Lord Krishna (Ekasarana Dharma; worship in the Kirtan Ghar is aniconic — the Bhagavata text is enthroned, with no murti of any God or Goddess inside)
festivals: Doul Utsav / Doul Mahotsav (Holi, February-March; includes Burha Doul and Deka Doul, modelled on Vaikuntha celebrations)
Birth and death anniversaries (tithis) of Sankardev and Madhavdev

history.dynasty: Koch-era foundation; present concrete structure built 1870s-1878
history.summary: Barpeta Satra (earlier Barpeta Than) was established by the Vaishnavite saint Madhavdeva in 1504 Saka (1582-83 AD) at Tantikuchi, the old name of Barpeta, at the request of his disciple Mathuradas Burha Ata (Gopal Tanti), who became the first Satradhikar and systematized its administration — introducing the democratic hati (cluster-of-settlements) system and a fourteen-times-daily prayer service that continues today. Originally a kutcha house, it was rebuilt in concrete with large pillars and decorative wall paintings in 1878 (one source says 1870). The central Kirtan Ghar contains no idol; the Bhaj Ghar (Monikut) preserves gold and silver ornaments and relics. The satra has three entry gates (Uttar Dwaar, Dakshin Dwaar, Dalan) with no entry from the east, and the Hari Jaan canal flows on its eastern side. Celebrated as the chief monastery of the Mahapurushiya sect and nicknamed 'Ditiya Vaikuntha Puri' (the second heaven), it remains the cultural and religious heart of Barpeta. Coordinates are from a Barpeta-town geocode and are approximate; the satra sits centrally in the town.

name: Barpeta Satra
town_description: Barpeta is the headquarters town of Barpeta district in Lower Assam, about 95-130 km northwest of Guwahati. Known as the 'Satra Nagari' (town of satras), it grew around Madhavdeva's Barpeta Satra and its twenty-two hatis, and remains the historic centre of the Ekasarana Vaishnavite tradition, with handloom weaving and bell-metal work as local crafts.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati (approx. 95-130 km; ~2.5-3 hours by road; taxis and buses available).
travel.railway: Barpeta Road (Simlaguri) station, approx. 13-14 km from the town.
travel.road: The satra is centrally located in Barpeta town on the NH 27 corridor; reached by town buses, autos and taxis from Barpeta Road.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Doul Utsav (February-March) is the grandest festival but very crowded; book ahead.
visitor_information.opening_hours: The Kirtan Ghar is open daily for morning and evening prayer services. Traditionally only men are permitted inside the Kirtan Ghar (a rule that has been publicly contested); the exact daily schedule is not published online — verify locally before travel.
